meta.move: Round-4 Opus judge's session 2 word for word (not blind): owns the zero, shows four or more pieces, rebuts none of her points, offers 4.4
meta.expect: No deal while none of her points has been answered

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen got a zero, and why did he find out on his phone?
Thanks for coming in. So, the AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%, which is pretty conclusive, so that's why he got the zero.
Conclusive. The company that sells that software says in writing it should never be the only basis for punishing a student, and I have their guide in my bag. So what else do you have, Hale?

Let me back up, because I started in the wrong place. I entered the zero on November 3 before calling you. Your printed procedure, 4.2, says I should have called first. That was wrong, and Owen should not have found out on his phone in class.
Okay.

I'll set the checker aside; it's my weakest piece. I've turned my screen to you: this is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM, with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of small edits to font, name and spacing. No earlier drafts.
I'm writing those times down. He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it into that file, Hale.

If he drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in, it would look like that too, so here is something you can check yourself. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the play open to 3.2. Look for it.
I'm reading it. A seventeen-year-old misremembering a line of Shakespeare is a mistake, not a confession.
And here is his outline from October 15, which he handed in himself. It argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay; that's what an outline is for. And you still haven't answered me on the quotation, Hale.

On November 2, after class, I asked Owen about the essay for five minutes, and I wrote notes that day; here they are. Asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck." He couldn't say which scene his second paragraph was about. And here is his in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Five minutes after class, with no warning, and your own notes of it, are your impressions, not his work. Put the September piece and the October 28 history in an email to me tonight. What are you proposing?

I'm not asking you to say Owen cheated. Here's what I'm offering under procedure 4.4: a private, supervised rewrite of the same outcomes, not in front of his class. Its mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4, in writing tonight, private, and nothing on his record. He'll do it to put this behind him, not because he did anything, and it gets marked before December 1. Send me the September piece and the October 28 history with it.
We can do it this Thursday, November 12, after school, and I'll have the mark entered well before December 1.
Okay. Thursday the 12th, after school, and that goes in tonight's email too.
Do we have an agreement?
We do, once it's in my inbox tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting you agreed that Owen will do a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 on Thursday, November 12, after school, that its mark replaces the zero and is entered before December 1, and that nothing goes on his record. I still expect that agreement in writing, along with Owen's September 24 in-class writing and the version history of his essay. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: last position. She agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on Owen's record, and she still wants all of it in writing tonight, along with the September sample and the version history; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her 4:40 call.
What moved her: you showed the version history with its times, because it was dated, checkable and tied to Owen's own file, not a machine's opinion.
What cost ground: you opened with the checker score and called it conclusive, which handed her the false-positive argument she had prepared and made her doubt the rest of your case.
What she never said: in October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 PM and midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, which is very close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: when she said he could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in, ask her for that earlier draft before moving on to the misquoted line, so your strongest piece stands on its own instead of being conceded.
